newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan sets 1997 GDP growth target at 6.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sets 1997 GDP growth target at 6.7 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's cabinet said on Thursday it had approved a long-range national development plan that sets a 6.7 percent target for 1997 gross domestic product growth.
The plan aims for average yearly GDP growth of 6.5 percent across the next 10 years, the cabinet said in a statement.
The growth target is highest for the subsequent four years at 6.7 percent a year, then eases to 6.3 percent between 2001 and 2006, the statement said.
Per-capita gross national product is expected to rise to US$13,971 in 1997 from a recent forecast of US$12,844 for 1996, it said. The official 1996 figure is due in late February.
For 1997, the cabinet set a target of 3.0 percent for consumer price growth, 2.5 percent for the jobless rate, 10 percent for export growth and 10.7 percent for import growth.
It set a 1997 target of 11.5 percent for growth of private fixed investment and 8.9 percent for growth of government fixed investment. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
